correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, 1<=r<n, L>0, a>b>0, 0<q<1, fixed geometric deposited amounts make the objective a constant plus r selected increments h(x). The derivative of h has exactly one positive zero. With c=q^r, h(x)/h(cx) decreases strictly from 1/c to 0: its logarithmic derivative is bounded above by -b(1-c)<0 through the elementary monotonicity of y/(exp(2y)-1). Therefore adjacent block differences cross exactly once at geometrically spaced loads, establishing all global optimization regimes and their tie cases. The golden-ratio subcase follows algebraically. A standalone checker replay passed 6089 supplemental assertions; neither finite tests nor numerical root finding is offered as proof.

value.rationale: The central ecological tradeoff is not an arbitrary invariant: pollen transfer depletes along a visitation sequence while recipient seed set saturates. For any numbers of flowers and high-receptivity recipients, the complete global optimal lineup collapses from binomially many assignments to a single sliding block, with all n-r exact threshold ratios 1/q and a directional reversal between scarce and abundant pollen. This provides an analytically interpretable benchmark for designed visitation arrays; its utility is explicitly limited by the idealized assumptions.
